targetTest: reminds after fifteen elapsed minutes despite a backward wall-clock correction
expected: After an initial warning, the next failure at thirty elapsed seconds is debug. A one-hour backward wall-clock correction does not delay the reminder: at fifteen elapsed minutes the next failure warns. Recovery logs once and a new failure warns as a fresh incident.
actual: The third failure at fifteen elapsed minutes logged debug instead of warn because failureLog subtracted the previous wall-clock warning timestamp from a wall time moved back one hour. Recovery and the subsequent fresh warning still logged as expected.
semanticAssessment: The active named regression compiled and executed exactly one case against unchanged production blob 4d724a609b5da08f31b7978396fd4d240c93fe70 from committed HEAD 8ab71cf7d53374f7b40003e77a68d6a75e0d7ec3. Its deepStrictEqual failed only at the elapsed reminder boundary: expected warn, actual debug. The case also asserted the initial warning, interval debug, single recovery, and fresh warning. This is the intended product behavior failure, not a build, fixture, runner, or environment failure. The test supplies a monotonic clock through a typed local options value; unchanged production ignores this extra field.
